title: Power BI - 58 Devices Labor Burn Dashboard (in progress)
blurb: End-to-end labor utilization dashboard modeling an A/E firm's FP&A workflow across three MTA contracts. Built a Python script to generate synthetic labor projections and Deltek Vantagepoint exports, reconciled the datasets in Excel via Power Query, and surfaced the output in a Power BI dashboard.
label: DASHBOARD
detail: Seed data has been generated. Currently performing excel reconciliation using Power Query. Power BI dashboard reconciling planned vs. actual labor on 3 separate contracts for the replacement of 58 MTA elevator and escalators, modeled on a real FP&A workflow at an A/E firm. Ingests weekly Vantagepoint Project Labor Exports (real Deltek schema), sub timesheets in intentionally varied formats, and supersession-controlled revisions of the labor projection. Power Query handles date parsing, employee normalization, functional group derivation, and report supersession and light VBA orchestrates refresh and validation. Vantagepoint exports are batch-processed weekly rather than consolidated, matching realistic weekly timesheets. Source data is accepted as-is and cleaned in the transformation layers. Built with anonymized data but with real firm names preserved. Employee names were anonymized using a python script and Faker library. Vantagepoint actuals were also randomly generated by a python script and the generation scripts are themselves deliverables demonstrating the data structures production would consume.

title: Power BI - Risk Register Dashboard
blurb: Construction risk register dashboard built around a Python update pipeline: dated entries written into the source Excel register are parsed and appended to a separate update table that powers the dashboard's trend and history visuals.
label: DASHBOARD
detail: Power BI risk register dashboard for a single-contract bridge and utility relocation project, built on PMBOK qualitative risk screening — a 5×5 probability-impact matrix using P × MAX(C,S) scoring with Low / Medium / High banding. Learning goals were on the data-architecture side: separating the register (the human-edit surface) from a Risk_Updates flat table (the time-series source), joined many-to-one on a stable risk_id key. A companion Python script handled append-only propagation — parsing new dated entries from the register's mitigation_log column and appending them as rows to Risk_Updates with year inference via a documented month rule. Power BI refreshed off both files via direct file connections; script appends flowed through without manual remodel.

New DAX patterns included disconnected axis tables to force every probability-impact cell to render including empties (SELECTEDVALUE-driven count measure); AVERAGEX with RELATED for the average-score trend across the to-one relationship — avoiding the bidirectional cross-filter trap; and a P × I cell-score measure driving rule-based heat coloring shared across three matrix variants — cost impact, schedule impact, and max impact, each with its own axis label table for dollar / duration / numeric scales. Page-level filtering on mitigation_status scoped active risks across all Page 1 visuals; a CALCULATE override returned the resolved count on the same page. A drillthrough Risk Detail page on the Top Risks table surfaced the full mitigation narrative and per-risk update history. Built with synthetic data designed to exercise every visual, not represent real project record.

title: Power BI - Agency Contingent Employee Staffing Tracker
blurb: A reporting tool built to manage a contingent staffing program placing personnel into agency roles.
label: DASHBOARD
detail: A Power BI reporting tool for a contingent staffing program. It tracks candidates from application through placement and shows the hiring pipeline, interview scoring, and the margin on each placement. It runs on a four-table model of roles, candidates, interviews, and status history, with Excel kept as the data entry layer so all calculations stay in Power BI.

Sorting the pipeline by stage needed a numeric sort key. Building that key as a DAX calculated column caused a circular dependency, so I learned to build sort-order columns as Power Query conditional columns instead, which compute before the data model loads. The candidate table also fanned out and showed each candidate against every role. I traced it to role fields being pulled straight from the Roles table and to two competing relationship paths, then fixed it by looking up role fields through each candidate's own role ID and correcting the cross-filter direction on the Candidates to Interviews relationship.
Late in the build I changed the main table from ranking candidates by interview score to ranking by gross margin per placement, which meant modeling the bill rate against the pay rate.

title: Power BI - Basic Expense Report
blurb: Built a Power BI dashboard aggregating employee expense totals by category with department, month, type, and employee name slicers as an introductory exercise while learning to use Power BI.
label: DASHBOARD
detail: Built a Power BI dashboard to consolidate and analyze corporate employee expense data, structured across two views: a summary aggregation page and an underlying transaction-level detail table. The summary view presents a matrix visual with employees as rows and expense categories as columns, with row and column subtotals and a grand total. The detailed view has four slicers (Department, Month, Expense Type, and Employee Name) that allow the user to filter the data dynamically. Used Microsoft's documentation for Power Query M to understand how to write custom column transformations beyond what the GUI displays

title: Full Stack Web Development - Weave
blurb: A travel planning tool built to demonstrate the ability to deploy a full-stack application. Additional features include the integration of google maps API and nodemailer.
label: WEB DEVELOPMENT
detail: Weave is a MERN stack group trip planning app developed. The app was launched in 1 week of development and implemented a Node + Express backend with a MongoDB NoSQL database. Users can search businesses and POI's using google autocomplete from google places, and pin them onto an interactive map

title: JavaScript + D3.js Single Page Application - Projectify
blurb: Rough order of magnitude estimate single page web application for Medical Office Fit-outs
label: WEB DEVELOPMENT
detail: A data visualization tool built to help commercial building owners and prospective tenants forecast tenant fit-out costs at the concept stage, before design documents are available. Users input square footage and select a construction type to generate rough-order-of-magnitude (ROM) projections driven by $/SF benchmarks compiled from completed medical office fit-outs. Results render on an interactive D3.js bar chart that allows real-time scope adjustment, giving stakeholders immediate visibility into cost drivers and value engineering opportunities. The tool reflects core project controls principles — historical benchmarking, parametric estimating, and visual reporting — applied to early-stage feasibility decisions where cost certainty is lowest and the impact of scope choices is highest.
